visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a black background featuring a stylized cartoon avatar in the top left corner. Large yellow and white text titles the sequence. A pink cartoon figure sits on the floor hunched over a glowing smartphone, with a thought bubble above indicating late-night usage. (2) A large white digit '1' transitions into the first fact. A white circular character with a blue object in its mouth appears. A male cartoon character in a grey shirt stands against a pink background, pointing upwards. Yellow text overlays the screen to define the psychological term. (3) A large white digit '2' introduces the second scene. The pink cartoon figure from the intro reappears, looking exhausted while staring at its phone. Red and white text boxes pop up to name the condition being described. (4) A large white digit '3' transitions to a short real-world television clip of a woman speaking. This is followed by an anime-style shot of a girl eating bread with an angry expression. Arrows and text markers appear around her to highlight negative traits. (5) A large white digit '4' shifts to anime clips of characters eating food rapidly. Various graphics of junk food like fries, milk tea, and fried chicken float onto the screen. Brightly colored emojis and text boxes emphasize the brain's control over cravings. (6) A large white digit '5' shows a figure with multiple thought bubbles containing 'Don't think'. A blue figure then appears with a thought cloud containing a white polar bear. A pink brain graphic is shown next to the polar bear. (7) The final phase shows the male cartoon narrator figure standing in front of a red circle logo. White text appears below the logo, and a yellow speech bubble with a hand icon prompts the viewer to interact with the screen.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a bright, high-tempo electronic BGM with a clear 4/4 beat. A male narrator begins speaking in a friendly, energetic tone with high articulation clarity. A soft 'whoosh' SFX underscores the title transition. (2) A clear 'ding' bell SFX marks the introduction of Fact 1. The narrator explains Hindsight Bias with a steady speech rate. Short 'pop' sounds sync with the appearance of text graphics on the screen. (3) Another 'ding' SFX signals the start of Fact 2. The narrator's voice maintains consistent arousal. The music continues in the background, keeping a steady energy floor under the vocal track. (4) A brief 'ding' SFX introduces Fact 3. The audio includes a half-second clip of a female voice from a TV broadcast. The narrator resumes with Fact 3. A cartoony 'boing' or emphasis SFX plays as traits are listed. (5) A 'ding' SFX marks Fact 4. The narrator discusses dopamine and junk food. High-pitched 'pop' SFX occur as individual food items are listed rhythmically to the music's beat. (6) A 'ding' SFX marks Fact 5. The narrator describes the white bear effect. A slight shift in vocal inflection occurs during the hypothetical instruction 'Don't think of a white bear,' followed by a 'pop' SFX. (7) The final phase features the narrator's call to action. A final 'ding' bell SFX coincides with the interaction prompt. The music swells slightly before a clean hard cut at the end.

It uses relatable scenarios (exams, late-night phone use) to explain complex terms like Hindsight Bias and FOMO, keeping the audience's attention with high-energy narration and rhythmic SFX.
